prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Paint an evening theatre box office in opaque gouache: a single small tangerine-orange paper admission ticket rests flat on a white cotton glove on the counter. The ticket is the very first thing the viewer sees at thumbnail size. Its clear small silhouette and crisp paper edge sit on a calm violet-gray fold. On another softly modeled fold, leave a little low-chroma pearl white beside the indigo-violet cast light so the glove reads as white cotton, with a soft stitched seam and matte cloth. The glove’s overall value stays quiet against the counter. Lose peripheral edges in the evening shadows; let the ticket be the only clean warm accent. Suggest the theatre ticket window in broad subdued shapes behind the still life. Visible opaque interlocking brush shapes and dry gouache edges.

Use case: illustration-story. Paint a dusk tea-house window in transparent watercolor. A single small red raspberry sits on a pale celadon glazed plate. Make the berry the first distinct thing the eye finds even at thumbnail size: a rich red cluster of tiny drupelets and one clear dark contact edge against a quiet pale blue-green area of the plate. Retain the plate’s own pale greenish turquoise through its body and shadow; show the amber window light as a thin warm translucent reflection crossing just part of the glaze. Soften the rim and keep bright sky and glowing window reflections subdued. Tea-house surroundings suggested with transparent layered washes, softened wet edges and watercolor paper showing through. Intimate still life with the fruit small relative to the plate.

Use case: illustration-story. Make a colored-pencil drawing of a carpenter’s workbench under a blue work light. A small yellow carpenter’s pencil is tucked into one pocket of a black leather tool pouch, its short exposed flat shaft and sharpened tip clearly shaped against the pocket, its lower end hidden behind the leather lip. The pencil catches the eye first at thumbnail size: keep the richest yellow and the crispest local contrast on that narrow accent. Convey the leather’s own black through broad near-black charcoal planes, fine grain and a curved pocket edge; the blue illumination skims the upper fold as a restrained muted reflection. Let the seams, workbench grain and surroundings recede in value and edge contrast. Visible layered colored-pencil strokes across textured paper.
